blocks.text: The Minsk life describes Vasily’s father’s death and his childhood employment in Saint Petersburg. He rises from shop errands to management and a fur business. His marriage to Olga includes the birth of son Nikolai and the death of their infant daughter. The couple supports churches, almshouses and patients who need care. Their eventual monastic vocation is presented as a mutual decision after decades of family and charitable life. The account prints April 13, 1866 New Calendar for his birth, while the OCA gives 1865.

blocks.text: Antonov’s reference entry records vows in 1920 as Varnava, priesthood in 1921, and the schema name Seraphim with his role as Lavra confessor in 1927. It dates the move to Vyritsa to summer 1930. These dated statements are separately attributed because the OCA says it does not know his first tonsure details and places settlement at Vyritsa in 1933 after imprisonment. The entries cannot simply be combined into one apparently uncontested chronology.

blocks.text: The OCA’s received life attributes clairvoyance and healing to him and describes visitors seeking consolation during illness and persecution. It also recounts searches of his cell and an attempted arrest stopped after a doctor warned of his condition. These are that source’s narrative claims.

blocks.text: The Minsk account records Nikolai’s arrest and execution in 1941 and identifies the elder’s wife, then schema-nun Seraphima, as his attendant until her 1945 death. It describes his prayer on a stone during the war as a reported feature of his life.

blocks.text: The OCA gives March 21, 1949 and explicitly supplies April 3 New Style. It describes weakness, remaining in bed and receiving visitors before repose. His death is not an execution; the title elder does not itself establish martyrdom.
